runtime: Ubuntu (Linux 5.15), bash 5.x, python 3.12, azure-cli installed. Offline unit tests run with python3 -m unittest; the dry-run was executed against a live tenant using an existing Azure CLI login.
procedure: 1. bash -n on the script. 2. python3 -m unittest tests.test_graph_readonly_app (6 cases: syntax, missing arguments, missing certificate file, ReadWrite refusal, FullControl refusal, and that a Read permission whose name contains 'Management' is not refused). 3. Run the script with --dry-run against a signed-in tenant and confirm it resolves the tenant and identity and lists the default permission set without making a change.
expected: Argument validation and the write-permission filter reject bad input before any directory call. The default permission set is read-only and passes the filter. --dry-run makes no change.
observed: All six offline cases passed. --dry-run printed the tenant id, signed-in identity and 12 permissions, and exited 0 without creating anything. An earlier revision of the filter used a '*Manage*' glob, which wrongly rejected DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All; the regression test now covers that case.
limitations: The apply path of this script has not been executed against a directory. The equivalent az ad app create / credential reset / appRoleAssignments calls were performed manually and succeeded, but that does not certify this script.
Re-run behaviour (reuse of an existing application and already-assigned permissions) is untested.
Failure handling when the caller lacks directory write access is untested.
No tenant identifiers are recorded here; the dry-run target is not disclosed.
